title: Does BPE actually win bits-per-BYTE at iso-FLOPs, and do bytes actually win spelling? BOTH INCONCLUSIVE at 0.2M params - BPE is 0.080 bpb ahead on the mean but one of three seeds flips the sign and the BPE arm's seed SD (0.109) is 5.5x the char arm's (0.020); the spelling probe moves the predicted way (+0.016 for bytes) at McNemar p=0.40. The sign-stable finding is the decomposition: at equal training BYTES the char arm is 0.087 bpb AHEAD, so BPE's iso-FLOP edge is throughput, not per-byte learning
hypothesis: At fixed training compute, BPE wins validation bits-per-BYTE because each forward pass packs ~2-4x more text, but a character/byte-level model wins a character-composition (spelling) probe because it is forced to model orthography explicitly.
question: At ~0.2M params on tiny-shakespeare, with training FLOPs equalised rather than steps: (a) does BPE-512 beat a 65-symbol char vocab on validation BITS PER BYTE, and does that survive seed noise; (b) does the char arm win a character-composition probe that BPE cannot win by lexical memory; (c) how much of any BPE advantage is data THROUGHPUT (more bytes per FLOP) rather than better per-byte learning; (d) does the advantage concentrate on words that cost many BPE tokens?
method: Two arms of an identical nanoGPT-style pre-norm decoder LM (2 layers, d_model 80, 4 heads, d_ff 320 GELU, learned abs positions, ctx 128 TOKENS, untied head) differing only in the vocab-facing matrices: (a) char/byte-level V=65, 175,040 params; (b) BPE V=512, 246,560 params, from a hand-rolled greedy merge loop (447 merges) fitted on the TRAIN SPLIT ONLY (approach reused from 2026-07-26_weight-tying-tiny), giving 2.220 bytes/token. tiny-shakespeare, 1,115,394 bytes, verified pure ASCII so 1 char == 1 byte exactly, 90/10 split. THE CONTROL IS ISO-FLOPS, NOT ISO-STEPS: fwd_flops_per_token = 2*[n_layer*(4*d^2 + 2*d*d_ff) + d*V] + n_layer*2*ctx*d (embedding LOOKUP free, output head counted as a real matmul, attention at the causal average over positions), train_flops = 3*fwd*tokens. The char arm's head is 80x65 not 80x512, so at equal FLOPs it gets 960 steps against the BPE arm's 800 (anchor) - and the BPE arm still sees 1.85x more BYTES (3.637M vs 1.966M), which is the mechanism under test. Achieved FLOP mismatch 0.045%. HEADLINE = validation BITS PER BYTE: total NLL in bits over the val text divided by the val BYTES actually predicted, never bits-per-token; evaluation is STRIDED (128-token windows at 50% overlap, only each window's second half scored) so neither arm is penalised by cold-start block boundaries - byte coverage 99.95% (char) / 99.97% (BPE). SPELLING PROBE: 144 val words (72 rare with train count <=3, 72 common with train count >=30, all >=6 chars); 3 distractors per word made by transposing an adjacent INTERIOR character pair (first/last char fixed) so every distractor has the identical character multiset and length - pure orthographic composition, not lexical frequency. Each arm scores the COMPLETE string context(96 bytes)+candidate under its own canonical tokenisation and must rank the true spelling first (4-way, chance 0.25); scoring complete strings sidesteps BPE's mid-word prompt-boundary problem entirely. Also reported: incremental bits-per-byte of the true word [logP(ctx)-logP(ctx+word)]/(ln2*len), and accuracy split by how many BPE tokens the word costs (measured with the BPE tokenizer for BOTH arms so the bins are comparable). FAIRNESS: lr swept PER ARM at seed 0 over {1.5e-3, 3e-3, 6e-3} on 240/200-step iso-FLOP-scaled probes with an automatic edge extension; it fired for both arms and both independently selected 1.2e-2. SECONDARY ISO-BYTES READING: both arms' curves read at the training-byte count the char arm actually consumed, which separates throughput from per-byte learning. 3 seeds x 2 arms main + 8 lr-probe runs, 564 s.
architecture: nanoGPT-style decoder-only LM, 2 pre-norm blocks, d_model 80, 4 heads, d_ff 320, ctx 128 tokens, untied head; char arm 175,040 params (V=65), BPE arm 246,560 params (V=512)

metrics.headline: val bits-per-byte at iso-FLOPs (char vs BPE-512) with a 3-seed sign check, plus a transposition spelling-probe accuracy and an iso-BYTES decomposition
metrics.SECONDARY_iso_bytes_verdict: char wins per BYTE of training text
metrics.SPELLING_PROBE_verdict: char (byte-level) wins on the point estimate, NOT significant

result_summary: BOTH LEGS INCONCLUSIVE AT THIS SCALE, WITH ONE CLEAN DECOMPOSITION THAT IS NOT. At 2.1139e12 training FLOPs matched to 0.045% (char 960 steps at V=65 vs BPE 800 steps at V=512, the char arm getting 1.20x more steps because its head is 80x65 not 80x512, the BPE arm still seeing 1.85x more BYTES), BPE-512 is 0.0795 bpb better on the 3-seed mean (2.6940 vs 2.7736) - BUT ONE OF THREE SEEDS FLIPS THE SIGN (per-seed deltas -0.158, +0.066, -0.147) and the BPE arm's seed SD is 0.109 against the char arm's 0.020, a 5.5x instability ratio, so the mean gap is 0.39x the BPE arm's own seed spread and Welch t on the seed means is -1.24 at df 2.1. The direction is the hypothesised one; the evidence is not there. THE SPELLING PROBE IS A CLEAN NULL IN THE PREDICTED DIRECTION: on 144 val words x 3 distractors made by transposing an adjacent INTERIOR character pair (identical character multiset and length, so lexical frequency cannot solve it), scoring COMPLETE strings context+candidate under each arm's own canonical tokenisation, char gets 0.9028 and BPE 0.8866 (+0.016 for bytes), paired McNemar 29 vs 22 discordant, p=0.40. Restricted to words costing 4+ BPE tokens - where the whole char edge lives - 0.862 vs 0.838, 28 vs 21, p=0.39. On words BPE spells in 2-3 tokens both arms sit at 0.993, i.e. the probe is at ceiling and cannot discriminate there. WHAT IS SIGN-STABLE AND IS THE POINT OF THE ROW: reading both arms' curves at the training-byte count the char arm actually consumed (1.966M bytes), char is at 2.747 and BPE at 2.835 - the char arm is 0.087 bpb AHEAD per byte of text. So whatever iso-FLOP advantage BPE has here is bought with THROUGHPUT (1.85x more text per FLOP), not with better per-byte learning; BPE simply reaches any given byte count for ~2.4x fewer FLOPs. Two smaller observations survive: BPE is MORE CONFIDENT YET SLIGHTLY LESS ACCURATE on the probe (mean true-vs-best-distractor margin 8.91 bits vs char's 6.67), and incremental bits-per-byte on the word itself splits by rarity exactly as the hypothesis predicts (rare words: char 3.974 vs BPE 4.097, char better; common words: char 2.778 vs BPE 2.712, BPE better). FAIRNESS AND ITS LIMIT: the lr was swept per arm with an automatic edge extension, which fired for both, and BOTH ARMS INDEPENDENTLY SELECTED 1.2e-2 - so neither is handicapped relative to the other, but neither optimum is bracketed above, and that aggressive lr is the most likely cause of the BPE arm's 0.109 SD. CAVEATS: 3 seeds; 2.0-3.6 epochs so both arms are still descending steeply; tiny-shakespeare substituted for enwik8 per the brief, and on this small repetitive ASCII corpus 447 merges only buy 2.22 bytes/token where a real BPE on enwik8 buys 3-4, so BPE's throughput advantage here is roughly half what the backlog assumed; at V=512 NO probe word was a single BPE token (min 2, median 4), so the backlog's single-token-vs-multi-token split degenerates into 2-3 vs 4+; the probe's canonical-tokenisation lower bound is looser for the odd distractor strings and therefore biases the probe slightly IN FAVOUR of BPE, so the true char edge is if anything a little larger than +0.016.

novelty_check.conclusion: PARTIAL-PRIOR-ART, and deliberately so: this is a replication-in-miniature of a settled comparison with one added control. ByT5 (2105.13626) established that byte-level models are more robust to orthographic noise and better on spelling-sensitive tasks while paying a throughput penalty. BLT (2412.09871) is the direct methodological ancestor of the control used here - a verbatim fetch confirms it is 'the first FLOP controlled scaling study of byte-level models up to 8B parameters and 4T training bytes' and claims better scaling for fixed INFERENCE cost. Both the metric (bits-per-byte) and the axis (bytes vs subwords under a compute control) are prior art; the abstract does not itself break out character/spelling results. WHAT THIS ROW ADDS: (a) the same accounting run 4+ orders of magnitude lower - 0.2M params, 2.1e12 FLOPs, 1M bytes - with the FLOP model written out term by term so the 1.20x step ratio can be audited; (b) an explicit ISO-BYTES reading placed next to the iso-FLOPs one, which separates 'BPE reads faster' from 'BPE learns more per byte' and is the only sign-stable result here (char +0.087 bpb per byte); (c) a spelling probe built to be solvable only by orthography (interior transpositions preserve the character multiset and length) and scored on COMPLETE strings so BPE's mid-word prompt-boundary problem never arises, with the tokenisation-lower-bound bias named as favouring BPE; (d) the NEGATIVE itself - at this scale the effect BLT and ByT5 measure is smaller than three-seed noise, and the larger-vocab arm is 5.5x more seed-unstable, which is a concrete boundary marker telling this lab that a 2-3 seed tiny-scale tokenizer comparison cannot resolve a 0.08 bpb effect. The 'no published version of this specific tiny-scale accounting' claim is a negative search result over 3 web searches plus 1 direct fetch, not an exhaustive review; arXiv/OpenAlex APIs 403 from this environment.
